# Enchantment control integration — provisional playtest

REVIEWED PROVISIONAL MANUSCRIPT. These NEW integration rules accompany seven approved rank-two Enchantment cards. The [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK2_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves the submitted body and records the binding interpretations below. Source originals remain preserved. This is not runtime certification, human balance approval, whole-game closure or GitHub delivery approval.

## Ordinary compelled Attack Actions

When an actual compulsion orders an ordinary Attack Action, use the target's native ordinary attack sequence, including inherent Extra Attack and an NPC's native Multiattack if that is actually its ordinary Action. No additional Action/attack is granted. A source expressly limited to one attack retains that limit: Confusing Flash is such an exception. An ordinary attack instruction is not permission to invent an Attack Action or convert another source's single attack into Multiattack.

Spend required ordinary ammunition normally. The command cannot activate consumable magic, special ammunition with a distinct expendable feature, RP/spellcasting, charges, recharge/per-rest abilities or optional finite-resource riders. Actual optional expenditures remain optional and cannot be compelled indirectly by choosing a method which requires them. Where instruction wording leaves the choice open, the target/controller may use a different legal ordinary method. If none satisfies the instruction, that instruction fails without spending a prohibited resource or manufacturing one. Existing source-specific limits and actual absolute prohibitions remain.

## Application IDs and independently scoped components

Each cast has a distinct application ID. Each component retains its own exact source/caster/target, application identity, deadline and actual defense state. Replacing one component never silently replaces another.

For Dire Charm, successfully established Charmed replaces only that caster's previous Dire Charm Charmed relation. Successfully established servant control replaces only the existing Dire Charm servant component across casters. Charmed-only and servant-only casts can therefore coexist. A successful repeat save, expiry or removal clears only still-active components originating from that application; an old application's save cannot remove a replacement component from another cast. Empty applications have no remaining save schedule. Core Charmed from other sources is unaffected. Shared hard-control history never refunds, even if a component is suppressed or replaced before acting.

## Compelled budget arbitration

This NEW rule resolves collisions among actual active mandatory instructions, including Command, Confusing Flash, Illusive Commands, Dire Charm and Crown of Madness. It does not create commands, extend duration, add repeated control to a one-turn source, grant new target permissions or override an explicit source-specific exception.

Record a priority timestamp for each specific instruction:
- Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands: successful establishment of that failed-save instruction.
- Dire Charm and Crown of Madness: issue of that turn's particular valid order, not the age of the underlying spell alone.
- Simultaneous instructions: underlying effect application order, then a stable source/mechanical ID as the neutral tie-break. Record it before resolving choices; do not decide a favorable order after outcomes.

At execution, gather still-active mandatory instructions and consider earlier priority first. A currently impossible/ineligible instruction claims no budget; proceed to the next. Compatible requirements can share one genuine legal execution. A single Action satisfies two instructions only if that same Action actually fulfills both. Once an earlier valid instruction claims an indivisible ordinary Action/interaction, an incompatible later instruction receives no second copy. Movement uses only the actual remaining movement allowance; sequencing instructions cannot reset spent movement or violate an earlier still-maintained posture/restriction.

A losing ongoing instruction is ineffective only for its contested budget/opportunity, not automatically dispelled. Its compatible independent portions may still operate within existing permissions. Its own endpoint, replacement and saves remain. Priority loss never refunds hard-control history. An invalid later order cannot erase an earlier mandate merely by being issued.

Example: Grovel and an Attack Action may both be satisfied if Prone uses only legal movement/posture and the attack remains legal. Two incompatible ordinary Actions cannot both be demanded from one Action budget. This arbitrates actual compelled behavior; it does not make compulsion optional or restore unavailable actions.

## Six-second control cadence outside initiative

This NEW cadence binds Dire Charm and Crown of Madness's ongoing order/end-save procedures. Other sources retain their actual timing unless expressly bound by a further review.

For a target with no existing initiative/control cycle, successful outside-initiative application begins a six-second virtual target cycle: first START immediately after resolution, first END six elapsed seconds later, then repeated six-second cycles. END resolves before the next cycle's START at the same boundary. Maximum duration remains the original absolute60-second deadline; expiry can end the spell before a later opportunity.

Reviewed procedure: a target shares one active virtual control cycle and one ordinary behavior budget across concurrent control applications. A new application during an already-open virtual cycle does not replay START or replenish budgets; its specifically allowed current-cycle END save still occurs. Each spell retains its own maximum deadline, components and saves. This treats application during an outside-initiative cycle like application during an existing regular turn, preventing repeated casts from creating extra immediate Actions.

The cycle supplies the bound spells' order opportunities, one ordinary six-second behavior budget where needed, and their repeat saves. It does not refresh encounter Reactions, recharge, resources, limited uses or manufacture extra combat turns. If actual combat order becomes necessary, establish ordinary initiative before any not-yet-committed hostile behavior; a virtual cycle is no permission for an extra pre-initiative attack.

Reviewed procedure for entering initiative: map the currently open virtual cycle to the target's first actual regular turn. Carry already received order opportunities and spent ordinary Action/movement/interaction budgets into that turn; do not replay or refill them at its START. The next still-unresolved END save occurs at that actual turn's END. Thereafter use actual regular starts/ends for future triggers. Keep the original absolute duration deadline. Do not replay already resolved virtual events. Existing effects begun in initiative retain their ordinary original virtual-marker rules if they later leave it; this bridge is for these effects first established outside initiative.

Application after an actual regular START grants no order for that already-started turn. A source explicitly permitting an affected current-turn END save still grants that save. Extra turns do not add order opportunities or repeat saves.

## Fixed-zone eligibility history

Calm Emotions and Zone of Truth have fixed spherical centers and require actual exposure/line of effect from that center. Geometric presence behind total cover is not yet eligible exposure. When cover opens around a creature still inside, that moment counts as its first eligible exposure.

Keep one save/acceptance result per creature per spell application:
- Calm Emotions: willing acceptance or the actual WIS save at first eligible exposure.
- Zone of Truth: the actual CHA save at first eligible exposure.
- Success: unaffected by that cast for its remainder, including later entry/cover changes.
- Acceptance/failure: the cast's existing effect is active only while exposed inside its zone; leaving or total cover suppresses it, and restored exposure resumes it without another save.

Acceptance is not a freely toggled dispel choice. Independent zones retain separate casters, concentration, histories and deadlines. Identical restrictions or suppression do not add numerical magnitude. Being unaffected by one zone does not make a creature immune to a different cast.

Calm Emotions suppresses actual Frightened effects, including a newly acquired Frightened source. Create and retain underlying records, ordinary clocks, maintenance and scheduled repeat saves. Once no valid suppressor remains, still-existing effects resume without replaying their original application. A condition which independently expires or is cured while suppressed does not return.

No emotion-themed name automatically disables a class ability. Actual Mooncursed, Momentum Rampage, Divine Fury, Fury of the Host and Beast Empathy source cards have no new emotion-maintenance requirement here. Their real Frightened rider on an affected recipient remains subject to suppression; other printed effects continue.

## Scope and open evidence

The instruction-priority, split-component and zone histories above are authored tabletop procedures, not executed stateful engine implementations. Concurrent outside-initiative applications and the first real turn's carried budget have exact manuscript approval; executable runtime integration remains open. Human testing remains necessary for multiple-attack compulsion, long control without concentration, fear suppression and the unchanged Zone of Truth class-price discrepancy.

## Binding interpretations from the exact review

One-shot Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands do not gain a new repeating cadence from this overlay. If their compelled behavior falls into the same current six-second/regular-turn opportunity, their demands compete for the same actual remaining behavior budget through Compelled Budget Arbitration.

Ordinary actual regular-start processing still happens at the first real regular turn: Reaction refresh, recharge, death-save and start effects follow their normal combat rules. Only the Enchantment control START/order opportunity and already-spent ordinary behavior budget are not replayed. The virtual START was not itself a combat turn or resource-refresh event.

For Illusive Commands, an independently valid soft movement/interaction component that survives a blocked hard Action component establishes a new instruction and replaces the prior pending same-spell record. A saved-against, wholly invalid or wholly blocked instruction establishes no replacement.

A Dire Charm application keeps its repeat saves while at least one of its original components remains. Once it has none, its save schedule stops; an old save never removes a later application's replacement component. No hard-control history is refunded.

Command's Grovel does not inherently consume the ordinary Action. Its required Prone posture can coexist with another legal Action. Confusing Flash's Attack branch continues to spend the ordinary Action on exactly one ordinary attack.

# Rank-three Enchantment integration — provisional playtest

REVIEWED PROVISIONAL MANUSCRIPT. This accompanies eight approved rank-three Enchantment cards. The [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves the submitted mechanics and marked completions. The existing [Enchantment control integration](ENCHANTMENT_CONTROL_INTEGRATION_PLAYTEST.md) remains authoritative in its approved scope. This approval does not certify runtime, human balance, whole-game closure or GitHub delivery. Cosmology remains outside this work.

## Dominate Beast: independent creatures and companion execution

NEW explicit binding: a Beast with an actual independent regular turn receives Dominate Beast orders at future regular STARTs, after ordinary start processing. Outside initiative it uses the reviewed shared six-second virtual control cycle. It shares the same actual budget with coexisting Dire Charm/Crown orders rather than creating another cycle. It has no repeat ending save, so virtual/real ENDs do not create one. Application after the current START grants no retrospective order. Existing ordinary real-start events still occur on entering initiative; already-received control orders/spent behavior budgets do not replay. The original maximum deadline remains.

A dominated Beast using the reviewed owner-attached companion chassis receives no independent turn. At its existing original owner's regular attached companion phase, the dominator may consciously issue a mental order for that opportunity. No extra caster Action/Bonus Action is charged. Actual Dominate Beast control must still exist, the companion must still be eligible and the command must obey its source profile and resource/behavior limits. Without a valid domination order, an already-valid owner command may execute, otherwise only ordinary uncommanded defensive behavior remains.

The forced execution occupies the ORIGINAL OWNER's shared command allowance for that numbered round and, if damaging/offensive under the existing chassis, its shared offensive allowance. These are structural caps; no unwilling owner's Bonus Action, RP or optional feature is charged. The dominator receives no new companion ledger. If another execution already consumed the command allowance, no extra commanded execution is created. If offense is unavailable but the command allowance remains usable, only a legal nonoffensive command can execute. An ordinary owner instruction is not a magical mandatory instruction and has no compulsion-priority timestamp; a valid domination order supersedes a contradictory owner instruction. An owner's already-paid Bonus Action is not refunded.

Reviewed completion — pending commands: redirecting a still-pending command for THIS SAME companion at THIS SAME attached phase reuses that existing execution's structural command reservation; it is not a second command. A still-pending offensive reservation on that same execution can cover the redirected ordinary attack; no duplicate offensive charge. If an existing reservation lacks offense, a new offensive redirection requires the still-free original-owner offensive allowance. Redirecting to a nonoffensive behavior does not refund an already-consumed/reserved offensive allowance. A reservation belonging to another companion, an already-completed execution or another phase cannot be stolen/reused to create this execution. Existing source-specific explicit release rules retain their scope; domination itself grants no refund.

Reviewed completion — phase availability: this bridge uses only a phase that the actual existing companion lifecycle supplies. It does not manufacture an owner phase after that lifecycle no longer permits one, duplicate it on an extra turn, or assign the companion the independent-Beast virtual control cycle. If no ordinary companion execution sequence is active and a commanded combat act matters, establish ordinary initiative with the source owner's existing companion phase. Noncombat work uses only the existing chassis's actual ordinary permissions and finite structural caps; the spell supplies no unbounded off-screen attack/action loop. Missing phase means no commanded execution, while concentration and absolute deadline continue. These bounded completions have exact manuscript approval.

The original companion profile, source-owner stat/DC rules, bond, ownership, slots, HP, Load, upkeep, summon duration, recharge and limited uses remain. Do not restore the original wild animal's discarded attack profile or substitute dominator levels/DC for its attack statistics. The spell's own INT application save uses its actual caster's spell DC. A phase checkpoint supplies no new regular START/END, Reaction refresh, death save, recharge or periodic/duration tick.

NEW exact completion: independent Dominate Beast casts retain separate applications and concentration. At a shared order opportunity their actual mandatory orders use Compelled Budget Arbitration, with timestamp at each order's issue and neutral same-time application/source order. A valid order never duplicates the actual creature/companion budget. Ordinary owner commands remain outside magical priority arbitration. No hard-control history is refunded if another instruction wins or an existing cap prevents execution.

## Hypnotic Pattern: atomic initial application

NEW spell-specific initial resolution:

1. Choose the perceived legal center using actual class-school range: Enchantment 60 feet, Illusion 30 feet; cube extends 15 feet on each axis.
2. Snapshot all creatures inside with actual center line of effect and actual sight of the pattern. Include self/allies when eligible; no selective omission.
3. Resolve each initial WIS save and determine each failed target's independently legal Charmed/Inc components and hard-control allowance.
4. Apply every target's determined initial components and immediate consequences. Actually applied Incapacitated ends that target's applicable existing concentration normally.
5. If the caster's own Incapacitated ends concentration on this Pattern, queue this Pattern's concentration teardown until every snapshotted target has received its initial application. Then remove all still-maintained components from this cast.

No target is skipped merely because it comes later in an implementation loop. Immediate loss of another target's unrelated concentration remains a real consequence even if Pattern then collapses. This is not a universal simultaneous-area or delayed-condition rule. It creates no late application for an initially prevented component.

Helper rousing ends one selected cast's Pattern application on one creature, removing both that cast's remaining Charmed and Incapacitated components. When a helper cannot distinguish multiple actual Pattern sources, use stable application order to select one, without revealing hidden source/caster metadata. Unlike ordinary Sleep's explicit shared wake, one Action does not rouse all Patterns. Positive post-defense/pre-temp-HP damage ends each actually affected Pattern application under its own damage trigger; it does not retroactively change the waking attack's hit/crit.

Recasts form independent sources under actual concentration transitions. An ordinary caster's old concentration ends before a new cast resolves; only a real multiple-concentration feature permits coexistence. Every new Incapacitated attempt checks hard history; independently legal Charmed may remain when hard control is blocked. Charmed-only applications gain no new repeat save. No general illumination, concealment, Speed 0 or ongoing entry aura is created by the persistent visual pattern.

## Terrifying Gaze and Slow: ending-save clocks

NEW explicit binding: Terrifying Gaze and both Slow modes have regular-target-END repeat saves, including an affected current regular turn's upcoming END. This save cadence is distinct from their maximum-duration endpoint. Extra turns grant no extra ending save.

If Terrifying Gaze begins outside initiative, ending saves occur at original application +6, +12 and +18 seconds; its maximum remains +18. An otherwise legally established Slow begun without a target initiative sequence uses ending saves every six seconds after application until its original 60-second maximum. This grants no new outside-sequence Transmutation Reaction trigger.

Reviewed completion — shared END-only cadence: unlike a commanded behavior cycle, these save schedules supply no START/order or action budget. On entering initiative, preserve already-resolved saves and the original absolute maximum. The first still-unresolved save opportunity maps to the target's next actual regular END, then actual regular ENDs supply future saves; never replay a resolved END or add an immediate transition save. If the deadline precedes that next END, expiry ends the effect first. Effects established in initiative retain their original regular/virtual markers on later exit under existing timing rules. This is the explicitly reviewed narrow transition for these new END-only schedules.

Temporary suppression of a condition/rider never pauses the underlying duration or scheduled saves. An actual successful save ends only that source's application on that target, not another independent cast.

## Slow: mode-specific commitments and overlap

Enchantment and Transmutation are separate actual class-school packages. One casting never receives their union. Both retain rank 3/base 5 RP and the preserved per-class level gates.

Transmutation's Reaction window occurs on a perceived creature's own actual turn, including an extra turn, at the beginning of a distinct voluntary movement segment or an Action after commitment and before the first movement step/main outcome. Moving, taking an Action and resuming movement creates distinct segments; choosing another square during continuous movement does not. Each foot/tile is not a trigger. The triggering creature MUST be selected and up to five additional legal perceived creatures may be chosen.

A valid committed Slow is independent of its parent. If a nested legal interruption removes the parent Action, the paid spell still resolves against still-legal chosen targets; it neither refunds nor cancels/revives that parent. The surviving parent continues after LIFO interrupts. Recalculate remaining movement before its next expenditure using actual current Speed and the unchanged spent-movement ledger. A no-Reactions rider bars future commitments only; a Reaction already legally committed in the stack is not canceled by that rider.

Enchantment's one-Action ceiling counts full Actions already committed on that actual turn. It blocks a future commitment once one is already committed, while an already-committed second Action finishes. Each actual extra turn has its own ceiling; the source grants no extra turn. Actual extra-Action resources may exist but cannot be newly committed contrary to the active ceiling. Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement and inherent attacks inside one legal Attack Action remain.

The Enchantment DEX rider is exactly -2 Dexterity ability checks/saves EXCEPT initiative; it changes no score/modifier, attack, damage, spell DC or unnamed derived value. AC gets its separate -2 only. Half-Speed uses existing strongest-adverse-Speed arbitration against the shared pre-control Speed, followed by the existing later systemic multipliers. Actual narrowly scoped defenses can suppress/block one component without erasing the others. Neither an Action ceiling retaining the ordinary Action nor Reaction denial claims whole-Action hard control.

Each source keeps its own concentration/save/deadline. Same Slow half-Speed/-2 AC/-2 DEX riders do not add magnitude. Distinct active Enchantment/Transmutation riders can coexist through separate casts; ending one exposes whichever other sources remain, not a merged permanent package.

## Suggestion: task scope and hard-control reservation

NEW binding: Suggestion's persistent mandatory instruction uses its successful establishment timestamp for Compelled Budget Arbitration. It retains that priority while genuinely active, but never supplies an extra budget or overrides an earlier applicable absolute restriction. Actual task permissions and reasonable legal details remain as authored on the card.

If the stated task necessarily requires whole ordinary Actions, including after an awaited conditional trigger, establish and claim the hard component once when Suggestion establishes. Do not reserve afresh per later Action. When blocked, only an independently meaningful legal soft task can establish. That surviving task may replace a prior Suggestion; an attempt with no legal meaningful task does not.

A task established without hard control cannot acquire it dynamically. If changed circumstances require an unreserved whole Action, seek an achievable reasonable path within the original soft permissions, such as waiting for an ordinary door opening. If none remains, end the remaining compulsion. Ordinary temporary delay/inconvenience is not itself cancellation. Neither caster nor target/controller may reword the task to create a new hard permission or extend its original eight-hour deadline.

An actually reasonable hostile task can direct the target's actual ordinary Attack Action/native attack sequence and required mundane ammunition; it does not compel optional finite features, special expendable ammunition, spells/RP or other forbidden expenditures. Reasonableness uses actual target beliefs/loyalties/knowledge/circumstances after payment without a caster diagnostic. Bonus Actions, Reactions and separately granted extra Actions are not commandeered. No repeating control cycle is added outside initiative.

## Scope and open validation

The companion pending-command/phase completions, independent Dominate Beast same-spell records, END-only transition, and Mental Chains voluntary-transport/plane completions on its card have exact manuscript approval. The Hypnotic Pattern batch is spell-specific. All prior 229 operational card records and actual source/class files remain unchanged. These are authored procedures, not executed scheduler or companion-control implementations. Human tests remain required for four-target Stunned, sustained native attacks, area Incapacitated, eight-hour Suggestion, no-repeat-save Fear and six-target Reaction Slow.

## Mental Chains: binding separated-plane interpretation

If a creature is involuntarily moved away from an application's anchor plane, that application's voluntary-distance/plane restriction has no effect while the creature remains separated. Ordinary rules govern further travel from that other plane, including voluntary travel elsewhere or return to the anchor plane. Concentration and the original deadline continue. On return, that application's original fixed anchor and boundary resume immediately. Another independent Mental Chains application on the creature's current plane still retains its own actual restrictions. This is the exact review's interpretation of the approved separation/resumption procedure, not a cosmology ruling.

# Creature companions: life, commands and identity

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED: 121 targeted checks and 2,800 Ranger conversion states.** This overlay discusses 100 exact passages from Druid, Mage, Mirrorsage, Ranger and Wizard, supported by five frozen common paragraphs. It closes no full class, form, temporary-HP system or complete runtime by itself. [Source register](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md), [source integrity](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json), [behavior checks](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json).

The original class cards and frozen class guide remain intact. The notebook's first classification, boundary reconciliation and event-model decisions are preserved in the audit folder. Where the historical first reply differs from the later boundary replies, the later explicit resolution controls. In particular, Auto-Raise is automatic, its new minion cannot act at all in the creation round, and Mirrorsage Charm was not in the older 219-source control closure.

## At the table

Keep one companion command and one offensive companion allowance per owner per numbered round, including multiclass companions and devices. A normal command costs your Bonus Action. A damaging companion action, or Mage/Wizard control action, spends the offensive allowance. A pure support command spends only the command. The earlier device ledger's internal field named `damage` now represents this shared offensive allowance; its public behavior remains compatible with existing device checks.

Issue ordinary commands during your regular turn. The selected companion moves and performs its command immediately after your whole turn, in an attached phase. It receives no extra independent turn. If it or its target becomes ineligible before execution, the command fails without refund. Your later incapacity or removal alone does not cancel an issued command; actual concentration/source ending can. Uncommanded companions can move defensively and Dodge, subject to their conditions; this grants no generic Reaction or autonomous attack/control.

Use the owner's original regular companion markers for recharge and previous/next-turn references. Extra turns, initiative changes and removal do not restart those markers. The attached phase's event-resolution checkpoint is distinct: it refreshes no Reaction, recharge, Action, death save or regular duration clock.

## Different kinds of creature life

| Creature | HP and 0 HP | Return and identity |
|---|---|---|
| Finite standard summons, Druid swarms, Mage Familiar, Mirror Beasts | HP-only bounded layer; at 0 disappear/end | No corpse, resource or free resummon; a new summon pays its actual source costs |
| Ranger Beast | HP-only; **NEW** immediate death at 0, no Wound checks, Stable or death saves | Actual animal and ordinary surviving corpse; death ends bond. No automatic resurrection or rebond |
| Mage Lich elite | Destroyed bound asset at 0; no usable corpse/resources | Same unique asset remains owned. Soulbound or actual completed LR can return it |
| Wizard standard undead | Destroyed at 0; consumed body never returns as new fuel | Ends on destruction, dismissal or owner's next completed LR, including Auto-Raised minions |
| Wizard elite | Supplied profile/cap only in this package | Binding/acquisition and return procedure are still missing; no create/bind/return API |
| Reflective Companion | Original creature's HP and life rules | Temporary control relation; no copied body, reset, new statistics or duplicate turn |
| Druid form | Same character's HP/life rules | Full forms and Buffer Reserve remain a separate open interface |

Companion healing restores legal normal HP only. It does not reset identity, duration, recharge, actions, source uses, effects or command budgets. Ranger's “heal normally” supplies no Hit Dice pool or automatic rest healing. The HP-only layer is specific to this reviewed companion chassis, not generic law for all animals/NPCs. Existing animal conditions, disease, poison, explicit injuries and timed effects survive bonding.

## Stats and ownership

**NEW:** finite created creatures snapshot base HP and AC at creation. Attacks, saves, class DC and S use the current values of the original source owner at resolution. Keep source owner, current controller, source class and creation source separate. A temporary controller does not donate their class levels, PB or attack bonus. The implementation rejects stats belonging to another owner/class; it provides no unrestricted transfer/rebinding operation.

## Ranger's persistent bond

Physical body identity is separate from current corpse eligibility. Keep one record whose state is living, corpse, consumed or removed. currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Charmed **Preserved Core text:** Cannot willingly harm the charmer; charmer has advantage on social checks against it. **Effect:** The creature cannot willingly take an action or make a choice it knows would harm the charmer: this includes attacks, harmful targeting, and knowingly placing the charmer in a harmful area or indirect effect. Unforeseeable or genuinely unknown collateral harm is not retroactively a willing violation. The charmer has advantage on social ability checks against it. Charmed itself never compels affection, obedience, beliefs, allegiance, affirmative protection or self-harm. **Application:** Each application identifies the charmer/source. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration and repeat-save/ending procedure. **Stacking:** A creature may be Charmed by more than one source; each source relation is tracked independently. Advantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Charm immunity prevents application. Forced actions from another effect are not made voluntary merely because the creature is Charmed. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 specifies the creature cannot attack the charmer or target the charmer with harmful abilities or magical effects, and gives the charmer advantage on social interaction checks. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Agency clarification: Charmed never by itself grants control over beliefs, targets or decisions beyond the explicit harm restriction. - Source-faithful correction reviewed in GPT_CUSTOM_RIDER_SECOND_REVIEW.md: Core's unwilling-to-harm restriction is broader than direct targeting; preserve its area/indirect-harm scope without importing mind control.
